traceability.notes:
All requirements and acceptance criteria for Story 010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION are fully implemented and verified.
Core functionality is provided by the valid-req-reference ESLint rule and its helpers: they parse story annotations, resolve and validate story paths, parse story file markdown to extract requirement IDs using a robust regex over the entire file, and validate each @req and @supports requirement ID against the extracted set. This directly satisfies REQ-DEEP-PARSE, REQ-DEEP-MATCH, and REQ-DEEP-ERROR, and ensures @req annotations point to actual requirements in the story content.
Quality standards around formats and structures are met by the regex-based extraction (REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+ across the full markdown), which is independent of sectioning or list style. Tests explicitly cover plain IDs and bullet-list requirements (story_bullet.md), as well as multi-story fixtures with shared and unique IDs (story_multi_a.md, story_multi_b.md). Because the extraction is content-wide, it naturally supports different story file structures (requirements sections, acceptance criteria lists, numbered lists, checkboxes) without additional parsing complexity.
Integration with existing validation is clean: the deep rule builds on the annotation formats enforced by valid-annotation-format (Story 005.0) and adopts safe path-handling patterns consistent with valid-story-reference (Story 006.0), while focusing solely on content-level requirement validation instead of duplicating file-existence checks. The rule wires into ESLint via a Program visitor that uses sourceCode.getAllComments(), respecting existing annotation parsing conventions.
User experience and error handling are well addressed: invalid story paths (traversal or absolute) produce a clear invalidPath message that includes the problematic path; missing requirements result in a reqMissing message that includes both the missing requirement ID and the story file path. File I/O and malformed content are caught and handled gracefully by caching an empty requirement set instead of throwing, ensuring the linter remains stable even when story files are missing, inaccessible, or malformed.
Documentation in docs/rules/valid-req-reference.md is directly tied to this story via @story/@req annotations and explains the rule’s purpose, behavior, and failure modes with concrete examples of correct and incorrect usage. Together with the focused Jest test suite and fixture files, this provides strong evidence that the story is fully implemented and currently passing all tests.
